headline: Revenue growth offset by merger costs and tax-benefit comp
summary_short: Essential Utilities' Q1 2026 revenue rose 10.0% y/y to $861.8 million on rate increases and gas-cost pass-throughs, but net income fell 20.9% to $224.4 million ($0.79 diluted EPS, down from $1.03) as merger-related costs and a non-recurring prior-year tax benefit weighed on the bottom line.
summary_long: Revenue grew 10.0% y/y to $861.8M as Regulated Water added $22.1M (rates, volume, acquisitions) and Regulated Natural Gas added $58.6M (mostly pass-through gas-cost recovery and rates). Operating income fell to $310.6M from $338.9M as O&M rose 27.6% ($38.0M), including $16.3M of pre-merger advisory/legal fees plus higher weather and employee costs. Net income dropped to $224.4M ($0.79 diluted EPS) from $283.8M ($1.03), mainly because Q1 2025 included a one-time $22.6M tax reserve release that didn't recur, swinging tax from a benefit to an expense. Operating cash flow fell to $265.4M from $299.5M on payment timing. The company issued $500M of 5.13% notes due 2036 and ended the quarter with $75.9M cash.
confidence_notes: REGENERATION: this run was invoked in force-regenerate mode; this write overwrites any prior WTRG_US_FY2026_Q1.json on disk (resolver reported summaryExists=false at run time, so no distinct prior version was diffed against). Date correction: the shard's stored eventDate (2026-03-31) is the fiscal quarter-end placeholder; reported_at above uses the 10-Q's actual SEC filing date (2026-05-07) per the 'real report dates' preference rule. Gross profit is a Yahoo-derived construct (Revenue − O&M − Purchased gas) rather than a line item Essential Utilities itself presents — regulated utilities don't report GAAP gross profit — but it reconciles exactly against the 10-Q's own O&M ($175.795M) and purchased-gas ($238.615M) figures, so it is retained with full confidence. Tax-rate swing: Q1 2026's effective tax rate (2.8% expense) versus Q1 2025's (7.8% benefit) reflects a $22.575M income-tax-reserve regulatory-liability release in Q1 2025 tied to the Aqua Pennsylvania rate order, which did not recur in 2026 — this one-off, not an operating deterioration, explains most of the y/y net-income and EPS decline. No forward guidance (revenue/EPS/capex ranges) appears anywhere in this 10-Q; Essential Utilities has a pending all-stock merger with American Water Works (announced 2025-10-26, exchange ratio 0.305 AWK shares per WTRG share, expected to close by end of Q1 2027), which plausibly explains the absence of standalone forward guidance during the pendency of that deal.

drivers.explanation: Rose $78.1M (+10.0%) as Regulated Water added $22.1M (rate increases, volume growth, and acquisitions) and Regulated Natural Gas added $58.6M (mostly pass-through gas-cost recovery and rate increases).

Fell despite the revenue gain as O&M expense rose 27.6% ($38.0M), including $16.3M of pre-merger advisory/legal fees, plus higher weather-related, employee, and insurance/bad-debt costs versus a favorable prior-year comparison.
Tracks the operating-income decline — the same O&M cost growth, led by merger advisory fees, outweighed revenue growth and the D&A add-back.
Fell 20.9% mainly because Q1 2025 included a one-time $22.6M tax reserve release (Aqua Pennsylvania rate order) that did not recur, swinging the tax line from a benefit to an expense.
Flows through from the lower net income; a larger diluted share count (283.6M vs 275.7M) added a small further drag.
Fell $34.1M y/y due to the timing of vendor payments and higher operations-and-maintenance expense.
Not broken out as a discrete driver in the release; cash built as $510.1M of new long-term debt proceeds, including the new $500M senior notes, outpaced capex and debt repayments.
Increase reflects the $500M issuance of 5.13% senior notes due 2036, used partly to repay commercial paper, plus $15.2M of low-interest government infrastructure loans.
Not explained in the release as a discrete driver; equity grew modestly as retained net income and stock issuances (DRIP, ATM, options) outpaced dividends and buybacks.

Revenue growth from rate increases and gas-cost pass-throughs was offset by merger-related advisory costs and a non-recurring prior-year tax benefit; the pending all-stock merger with American Water is targeted to close by the end of Q1 2027.
